open_points.subject: service API listener in an owner-only start
open_points.text:
Registry serves
each surface on a listener of its own, at its configured address, and
decides nothing about reachability beyond that listener's own form — bound
exclusively, an IPv6 one for IPv6 alone (A17 rule 1).
open_points.question: Does this statement apply only when the service API is configured, or must an owner-only start also open a service API listener despite A17 rule 1 saying it opens none?
options: Qualify the statement: each enabled surface has its own listener; an owner-only start has only the owner-interface listener.
Require both listeners on every start and remove A17's owner-only mode.
Treat the service API as a surface even when it has no configured address and no listener.
open_points.default_guess: Qualify it so that each enabled surface has its own listener and an owner-only start opens only the owner-interface listener.

witness.initial: All required owner-interface configuration is valid, and none of the four service tokens or the service API address is set.
events: The host administrator starts Registry in the owner-only configuration allowed by A17 rule 1.
A service client attempts to connect to the service API address while the owner uses the owner interface.
outcomes: The changed State 3 passage says each of Registry's two surfaces is served on its own listener at its configured address, although this configuration supplies no service API address.
A17 rule 1 says Registry serves the owner interface alone and opens no service API listener, so the service client's connection reaches no Registry.
witness.observer: The host administrator and the service client
